sections.overview: The western barn owl is a pale, mostly nocturnal owl that hunts over open country.
sections.identification: Its heart-shaped facial disc, dark eyes and pale underside make it distinctive.
sections.habitat: It hunts over farmland, grassland and wetlands and often roosts or nests in barns, lofts and church towers.
sections.diet: In Europe, small mammals—especially voles—make up most of its prey.
sections.behavior: It can locate prey by sound and regurgitates indigestible remains as pellets.
sections.reproduction: It nests in dark cavities or buildings, and the number of eggs can vary with food availability.
sections.ecology: Its dependence on small mammals links it closely to open agricultural mosaics and grasslands.
sections.conservation: Closing access to old barns and towers can remove nesting sites, so suitable cavities and nest boxes can help locally.
